Nickel foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF) (20 mm × 20 mm × 0.42 mm) was cleaned by sequential treatment with 2 M HCl solution, ethanol, and deionized water for 10 min.
nodes.source_text: nickel foam (NF) (20 mm × 20 mm × 0.42 mm) was cleaned by sequential treatment with 2 M HCl solution, ethanol, and deionized water for 10 min

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: The cleaned nickel foam was used as the working electrode in a three-electrode system with a graphite rod as counter electrode and saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as reference electrode. The electrolyte was a mixture of 9 mM Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 3 mM Fe(NO3)3·9H2O. A constant cathodic current of 2 mA cm⁻² was applied to the working electrode for 1 h. The product coated on NF was cleaned thoroughly using ethanol and distilled water several times and dried in an oven at 60°C for 12 h to obtain the pristine NiFe-LDH sample.

nodes.name: Tungsten doping and corrosion of NiFeW1-LDH
nodes.procedure: The freshly made NiFe-LDH sample was immersed in 1 mM WCl6 ethanol/water solution (ethanol/water volume ratio of 1:1) at 25°C for 3 h. The solution was stirred by a magnetic stirring device during immersion. After immersion treatment, the sample was washed and dried to obtain NiFeW1-LDH.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH at various temperatures
nodes.source_text: The anodic polarization curves after 90% iR_s correction, the Tafel fitting curves (η-log i), and the fitting parameters of the electrocatalysts in 1 M KOH are shown in Fig. 4a, b and Table 1, respectively. The overpotentials at 100 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀₀) of NiFeW₁-LDHs, NiFeW₃-LDHs, and NiFeW₅-LDHs are 292, 256, and 278 mV, respectively, which are much smaller than that of NiFe-LDHs (337 mV).
The overpotentials at 100 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀₀) of NiFeW₁-LDHs, NiFeW₃-LDHs, and NiFeW₅-LDHs are 292, 256, and 278 mV, respectively, which are much smaller than that of NiFe-LDHs (337 mV).

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH with comprehensive electrochemical characterization
nodes.source_text: The representative NiFeW₃-LDHs exhibit remarkable OER electrocatalytic activity with a low overpotential (211 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²), a small Tafel slope (36.44 mV dec⁻¹), and fine stability (more than 120 h at 10 mA cm⁻²). The chronopotentiometric curves for 120 h at 10 mA cm⁻² of all four electrocatalysts illustrate a stable overpotential. NiFeW₃-LDHs demonstrate the lowest platform overpotential, and its polarization curves before and after 5000 CV cycles show no significant changes. The Faraday efficiency (~100%) of O₂ production for NiFeW₃-LDHs agrees well with the theoretical yields.
The overpotentials at 100 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀₀) of NiFeW₁-LDHs, NiFeW₃-LDHs, and NiFeW₅-LDHs are 292, 256, and 278 mV, respectively, which are much smaller than that of NiFe-LDHs (337 mV).

nodes.description: Double-layer capacitance measurement via cyclic voltammetry in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: To further study the influence of corrosion and W doping on the active site number of the OER electrocatalyst surface, a narrow potential range of the double capacitance potential region was selected, and CV curves were obtained with various sweep rates. The Cdl value of the optimized NiFeW3-LDHs is ~1.5 times that of NiFe-LDHs, demonstrating that NiFeW3-LDHs possess more active sites and better OER electrocatalytic activity.

nodes.description: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) in 1.0 M KOH at 1.58 V
nodes.source_text: For the Nyquist plots at 1.58 V (overpotential of 350 mV) of the electrocatalysts in 1 M KOH, two arcs are observed in the entire frequency region of the Nyquist diagram. The arc in the middle- and high-frequency regions of the Nyquist complex plane is related to the physical response of the pore structure on the electrocatalyst surface, while the arc in the low-frequency region characterizes the electrochemical reaction process on the interface of the electrocatalyst and the electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform and consistent growth of layered nanosheets for pristine NiFe-LDHs. NiFeW₁-LDHs display wrinkled nanosheet assemblies with fine corrosion cracks. NiFeW₃-LDHs exhibit different sizes of nanopores on the surface. NiFeW₅-LDHs show stacking and flocculent nanosheet structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pristine NiFe-LDHs display uniform and consistent growth of layered nanosheets (Fig. 2a). The NiFe-LDHs surface change obviously after etching with various concentrations of WCl₆ solution. There are wrinkled nanosheet assemblies and fine corrosion cracks on the NiFeW₁-LDHs surface (Fig. 2b). However, there are different sizes of nanopores on the NiFeW₃-LDHs surface (Fig. 2c)... stacking and flocculent nanosheet structures are observed on the NiFeW₅-LDHs surface (Fig. 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mappings of NiFeW₃-LDHs show that Ni, Fe, W, and O elements are homogeneously distributed on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ...the corresponding energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mappings of NiFeW₃-LDHs illustrate that the Ni, Fe, W, and O elements are homogeneously distributed on NF (Fig. S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show strong characteristic peaks of nickel foam in all samples. Due to lower contents of NiFe and NiFeW hydroxides compared to nickel, the hydroxide phase is not observed in the XRD patterns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Strong characteristic peaks of Ni foam are detected in the XRD patterns of the samples (Fig. 3a). However, due to the lower contents of NiFe and NiFeW hydroxides compared to those of Ni, the hydroxide phase is not observed in the XRD patterns.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectra show broad and strong absorption peak at 3379 cm⁻¹ for stretching vibration of -OH interlayer water molecules, weak absorption peak at 1629 cm⁻¹ for bending vibration of interlayer water, and asymmetric stretching vibration of CO₃²⁻ at 1359 cm⁻¹, confirming the formation of LDH structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The broad and strong absorption peak at 3379 cm⁻¹ belongs to the stretching vibration of -OH interlayer water molecules, and the relatively weak absorption peak at 1629 cm⁻¹ belongs to the bending vibration of interlayer water (Fig. 3b). The asymmetric stretching vibration of CO₃²⁻ is observed at 1359 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p spectrum of NiFe-LDHs shows spin-orbital peaks at 855.5 and 873.2 eV attributed to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂, with satellite peaks at 861.5 and 879.6 eV. NiFeW₃-LDHs display positive shift (~0.3 eV) in Ni 2p peak position compared to NiFe-LDHs, indicating W doping modulates electronic density of Ni and enhances higher valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum of (NiFe-LDHs) show spin-orbital peaks at 855.5 and 873.2 eV which are attributed to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂, respectively (Fig. 3c). The peak position of Ni 2p (2p₃/₂, 2p₁/₂) for NiFeW₃-LDHs displays a positive shift (~0.3 eV) compared with NiFe-LDHs, illustrating that W doping modulates the electronic density of Ni and enhances the higher valence state of Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Fe 2p spectrum of NiFe-LDHs shows two main peaks at 712.2 and 725.5 eV corresponding to Fe 2p₃/₂ and Fe 2p₁/₂, indicating Fe³⁺ valence state. NiFeW₃-LDHs shows Fe 2p peak shift to higher binding energies (~0.2 eV), indicating higher valence state of Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe 2p spectrum of NiFe-LDHs has two main peaks at 712.2 and 725.5 eV, corresponding to Fe 2p₃/₂ and Fe 2p₁/₂, respectively, indicating the valence state of Fe³⁺ (Fig. 3d). Additionally, the Fe 2p peak of NiFeW₃-LDHs shifts to higher binding energies (~0.2 eV) compared with NiFe-LDHs, indicating that the higher valence state of Fe existed in NiFeW₃-LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS W 4f spectrum shows two spin-orbital peaks at 37.3 eV (W 4f₅/₂) and 35.2 eV (W 4f₇/₂), belonging to W⁶⁺. W 4f binding energy of NiFeW₃-LDHs shifts negatively by ~0.2 eV compared with WO₃, indicating oxidation state of W⁶⁺ decreases due to interaction between W, Ni, and Fe elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ...the W 4f spectrum shows two spin-orbital peaks at 37.3 eV (W 4f₅/₂) and 35.2 eV (W 4f₇/₂), belonging to W⁶⁺ (Fig. 3e). Compared with that of WO₃, the W 4f binding energy of NiFeW₃-LDHs shifts negatively by ~0.2 eV, indicating that the oxidation state of W⁶⁺ decreases.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS O 1s spectra show characteristic peaks corresponding to metal-oxide bonds (M-O), oxygen vacancies (V_O), metal-hydroxide bonds (M-OH), and adsorbed water. Peak area ratio of V_O in NiFeW₃-LDHs (39.6%) is higher than NiFe-LDHs (33.1%), NiFeW₁-LDHs (35.3%), and NiFeW₅-LDHs (38.2%), indicating W addition effectively enhances V_O concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ...the characteristic peaks in the O 1s spectra correspond to metal-oxide bonds (M-O), V_O, metal-hydroxide bonds (M-OH), and adsorbed water (Fig. 3f). The peak area ratio of V_O in NiFeW₃-LDHs (39.6%) is higher than those of NiFe-LDHs (33.1%), NiFeW₁-LDHs (35.3%), and NiFeW₅-LDHs (38.2%), indicating that the addition of W effectively enhances the V_O concentration in NiFeW₃-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectral intensity of NiFeW₃-LDHs is much higher than those of NiFe-LDHs, NiFeW₁-LDHs, and NiFeW₅-LDHs, indicating W content influences V_O concentration and affects OER performance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR spectral intensity of NiFeW₃-LDHs is much higher than those of NiFe-LDHs, NiFeW₁-LDHs, and NiFeW₅-LDHs (Fig. S4), indicating that the W content influences the V_O concentration, thus affecting the OER performance of NiFeW₃-LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determined the content ratios of metal elements in each sample: NiFe-LDHs (Ni₆₅Fe₃₅), NiFeW₁-LDHs (Ni₆₁Fe₃₂W₇), NiFeW₃-LDHs (Ni₅₈Fe₃₀W₁₂), and NiFeW₅-LDHs (Ni₅₅Fe₂₇W₁₈).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The content ratios of metal elements in each sample were determined by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). The elemental ratios in NiFe-LDHs, NiFeW₁-LDHs, NiFeW₃-LDHs, and NiFeW₅-LDHs were Ni₆₅Fe₃₅, Ni₆₁Fe₃₂W₇, Ni₅₈Fe₃₀W₁₂, and Ni₅₅Fe₂₇W₁₈.
